quarterly_data.signal: Volozh laid out the full price waterfall per megawatt, including the levels below and above Nebius' own contracts. Bare metal: 'we started selling like everybody else, bare metal prices were at the level of 10, maybe $15 million per megawatt'; retail/core cloud 'the next level of $20, $25 million per megawatt'; short-term capacity '$40, $50 million per megawatt'. Above that, neoclouds 'sell it at $10, $15 to people who then sell it to companies developing applications at $20, $30, sometimes $50 short term', and at the token layer 'Anthropic tokens recalculated per megawatt is something like $100 per megawatt', while the end-industries using those tokens 'generate value per megawatt, which is much higher than this $100, maybe $200, maybe $500 per megawatt'.
quarterly_data.figure: bare metal 10, maybe $15 million per megawatt; core $20, $25 million; short-term $40, $50 million; Anthropic tokens something like $100 per megawatt; end value $200, maybe $500 per megawatt

quarterly_data.signal: Build-rate ambition raised above the previously stated pace and sized against the industry: own cloud capacity is 'just close to a gigawatt of capacity this year, and we want to build something like a gigawatt a year, and then probably eventually more, a gigawatt and a half, 2 gigawatts a year.' Industry context: capacity built was '5 gigawatts a couple of years ago. It is now 10 probably this year. It will be 15, 20 gigawatts a year built in 2027, 2028. So we are probably, I do not know, 5%, 10% market share in the world.' Volozh argued 'GPU cloud, unlike previous classical cloud, is probably 10 times larger. It's a trillion-dollar revenue business.'
quarterly_data.figure: close to a gigawatt this year -> a gigawatt a year -> a gigawatt and a half, 2 gigawatts a year; industry 10 GW this year to 15, 20 gigawatts a year in 2027, 2028; Nebius 5%, 10% market share

quarterly_data.signal: Financing gap behind the 5 GW contracted-power target quantified for the first time: 'We announced 5 gigawatt. It is easy to announce. We signed it, 5 gigawatt. We have this capacity to build. To launch 5 gigawatt multiplied by $50 billion per megawatt, it is $250 billion of financing. So far, we financed maybe 20% of that. We need another $50 billion and then another $50 billion.' [Verbatim quote; the per-megawatt unit is evidently a slip of the tongue — 5 GW = 5,000 MW x $50 MILLION per MW = the $250 billion he states, and his own price waterfall earlier in the same session is quoted in millions per megawatt.] Company history framed as '$40 billion raised later, five gigawatts contracted later', from a starting point of one 10 megawatt data center and $2.5 billion of cash.
quarterly_data.figure: $250 billion of financing needed for 5 gigawatt; maybe 20% financed so far; another $50 billion and then another $50 billion; $40 billion raised to date

quarterly_data.signal: Permitting/community pushback is slowing the industry and Nebius is answering it with geographic diversification and an open-construction model. 'Specifically this year, there is a lot of delays in the industry.' Nebius builds 'not only in the U.S., we build a lot in Europe. I think we're the largest builder in Europe. We build in the Middle East. We build in India, in Japan now through partnerships.' Unlike U.S. peers whose sites were 'under NDAs', Nebius arrives openly, builds a booth showing the project, runs community education programs and employs local unions. Example cited: a France site on the brownfield of an old Bridgestone tire factory.

Volozh set out why the full-stack model matters versus pure bare metal: 'Otherwise, we would be just like any other neocloud. We would be just providing bare metal services at USD 10 million per megawatt to people who really then make a product with OpenAI, Anthropic, or Microsoft, whatever, Google. Instead, we can build our own full stack and our own product and sell it much higher level with materially different margins. You can see the prices, it's 2 or 4 times higher.' He conceded product quality is not yet the differentiator — 'you can sell everything which is built' — but expects supply and demand to balance in 'a year, in 18 months, or 20, 22 months, 24 months', after which customers will start comparing products.
quarterly_data.figure: bare metal USD 10 million per megawatt vs full-stack pricing 2 or 4 times higher

contracts.signal: Volozh on the Meta relationship: 'Actually, we're building for Meta now. Their second contract comes in Q1, Q2 next year.' He added that if Meta decided to put unused capacity on the market, 'we were the first to beg them to give it to us because we will take this bare metal and resell it on the model level with much higher value. I don't know, maybe we'll be able to offer them some backstops if they offer us this capacity.' The Meta and Microsoft contracts are described as bare-metal deals ('It is not our core business... They need just bare metal') used to finance Nebius' own core cloud build rather than as the core business.
contracts.type: capacity contract (second contract onlining Q1, Q2 next year)
